findings.claim: The claimed acyclic intent construction is internally undefined: PlannedIntentBodyCommitment includes the deterministic intent path before the final intent hash/path is derived, while ExecutionTransitionIntent is required to be content-addressed.
findings.evidence_excerpt: That domain includes source hash/version, previous completion head/sequence, edge, attempt/count invariants, reservation, deterministic intent ID/path, writer/authorization IDs, and candidate-template hash
findings.impact: No byte-exact validator can prove the stated order without either a hash/path cycle or an unstated non-content-addressed path rule; different implementations can bind OPEN and P3 to different intent identities at the charge boundary.
findings.recommended_action: Separate a pre-hash logical intent ID from the content-addressed path, exclude the latter from the body commitment, derive it only from the finalized intent hash, and pin that exact derivation in the fixture and validators.

findings.claim: P3 does not admit the charged completion-corruption recovery that Section 9.1 requires: that recovery makes a CompletionCorruptionTombstone the next P3 source even though P3's closed exceptional-link list omits such a record and every next intent otherwise requires a completion-chain head.
findings.evidence_excerpt: then uses the tombstone as the sole P3 source for one guarded same-attempt terminal transition
findings.impact: After a partial or differing charged APPLIED completion, the terminal transition cannot satisfy ordinary P3 without either bypassing the closed lineage validator or inventing an undeclared exceptional link, so the charged attempt can remain unrecoverably open or be closed with unreviewed charge semantics.
findings.recommended_action: Define a charged CompletionCorruptionRecovery lineage record with predecessor head/hash/sequence, preserved attempt and charge, tombstone and RECOVERY_CLOSE bindings; make it the monotone next chain head and explicitly admit only that record in P3 before the terminal transition.

findings.claim: The post-charge exhaustion branch has no executable accounting transition: reservation R and its retry IDs are immutable and no-refund with all usage constrained to A <= R, yet exhaustion is said to be recoverable by a fresh HUMAN ceiling/recovery decision without defining a new allocation or how it binds the already-open intent.
findings.evidence_excerpt: exhaustion requires a fresh HUMAN ceiling/recovery decision and never permits a new admission cycle to reuse the charged attempt
findings.impact: Once a legitimate charge exhausts the fixed reservation or append count before completion/index closure, the declared pairs cannot spend more and new pairs are not authorized; recovery therefore either strands the charge or requires undeclared, unaccounted effects.
findings.recommended_action: Define a HUMAN-authorized post-charge recovery-allocation record and deterministic ceiling arithmetic that preserves the original reservation, binds the same attempt/open intent, authorizes new bounded pair IDs, and is accepted by P3/P15; otherwise declare exhaustion terminally fail-stop instead of recoverable.
